questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/e2065775ae6372e8c820b5e2f19f6f105e032dcd37db1e32e04af5bfa6a4faf9.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $x\in (-3,-2]\cup (2,4)$
- $x\in (0,2]$
- $x\in [1,4)$
questions.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is invertible on the intervals $x\in (-3,-2]\cup (2,4)$ and $x\in (0,2].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/3c5bc724ee29aee7bef2790012bf0e73ce1ed087134213dbad36a670fd136a36.png)

        

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $[1,4)$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/03b9d70513a4ef99b39c9f05d0c0ac803f8e5611d0967015e9c1d9c0f45bd418.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and II only".

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?
questions.worked_solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/c728d173c13a1e7b3bcad0e9f0284c97f2ca075c795dcb1f38ed086c19cc0504.png)

From the above, we see that: 

- For graphs I and IV, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graphs I  and IV show one-to-one functions. This means that  these functions are invertible.

- For graphs II and  III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. So, these are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=-{x}^{2}+1,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,0]$
- $x\in (-2,2]$
- $x\in (-2,\infty )$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=-{x}^{2}+1$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

- Reflect its graph across  the $x$-axis to get $y=-{x}^{2}.$

- Finally, translate $y=-{x}^{2}$  by $1$ unit up to  get $f(x)=-{x}^{2}+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/83a9f5966c76b89b2cad9c6244e2e447fb0052fc7f946df954df76265628c4a7.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

*The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,0].$ On this interval, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/f694b6b1bc979289b748758385e05575990bd866457e75a84fbf7bdf335c03b9.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-2,2].$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once. Since  $(-2,2]$ is a subset of $(-2,\infty )$, our function is not invertible on $x\in (-2,\infty )$ either.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/c03118f3fd0193910b49e26ab5ea56e4320fd23583feb3267cd4442d0a157583.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=2x+4,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$
- $x\in (10,\infty )$
- $x\in [-5,5)$
questions.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is a linear function with slope $2$ and $y$-intercept $4,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/d33314230419ec762bc4ad8603b2e6c3436461cd6b4b6fe4783d12a23d01b660.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ On this interval, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- Since the function is invertible on $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ it is also invertible on  $x\in (10,\infty )$ and $x\in [-5,5).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".

Determine the largest domain on which the function $f(x)$ (shown above) is invertible.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain of our function is $x\in [-3,5].$ 

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ does not pass the horizontal line test on the interval $x\in (1,3).$ In this case, the horizontal line $y=1$ intersects the graph at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/eb544795c61be7dd87568e6def10fc907c3554b603c3b344f88ac2a8ff847f8d.png)

- Among the given options, the largest domain on which the function $f(x)$ is invertible is $x\in [-3,1]\cup (3,5].$ On this domain, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980752/assets/4059a1ad684023640358af6ee38f0967957336578eb93b3299c9c842e7ce108f.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is $x\in [-3,1]\cup (3,5].$
